title: Pre-Operative fSRS for Brain Metastases
official: Improving Outcomes in Patients With Metastatic Cancer to the Brain With Pre-Operative Fractionated Radiosurgery (fSRS): A Pilot Study
summary:
This pilot study investigates a new approach for patients with metastatic cancer that has spread to the brain (brain metastases) who are already planned to receive both fractionated stereotactic radiosurgery (fSRS) and brain surgery as standard treatment for their condition. Usually, surgery comes first, followed by radiation. However, post-operative radiation can sometimes lead to the cancer returning in the area, spreading to the brain's lining (LMD), or causing side effects from radiation (RN). This study hypothesizes that delivering fSRS before surgery may improve outcomes by enabling more accurate targeting, reducing tumor spillage, and potentially decreasing RN, while improving treatment compliance. The study is specifically testing the sequence of these two standard treatments.

This is a single-arm, prospective study enrolling 12 adult participants (age \>18) with 1-5 brain metastases, where one main tumor (between 2.0-5.0 cm diameter) requires surgical resection. Participants will receive fSRS (27 Gy in 3 fractions) approximately one week prior to surgery, as part of the study's approach. Throughout the study, participants will also have regular brain MRI scans to monitor their condition and complete tests to check memory and thinking skills (like the MoCA test) at various points.

The main goal is to see how well the cancer is controlled at the surgery site (called local freedom from progression, or FFP) over 6, 12, 18, and 24 months post-operatively. Secondary outcomes include rates of LMD and RN. Safety (adverse events, toxicities) will be continuously monitored by an independent Data Safety Monitoring Committee (DSMC). Each participant will be in the study for 2 years.

This research aims to provide preliminary data to inform future larger, randomized trials, ultimately improving treatment strategies for patients with metastatic brain cancer.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patient is ≥18 years old.
* Radiographic confirmation of 1-5 brain metastases by MRI with contrast obtained within 4 weeks prior to registration. One of these must be an index lesion requiring surgical resection.
* The maximum diameter of the index lesion, as measured on any orthogonal plane (axial, sagittal, coronal) on the post-contrast MRI, must be ≥2.0 cm and ≤5.0 cm.
* Documented pathological diagnosis of active or history of invasive cancer within the past 5 years.
* All brain metastases must be located ≥5 mm from the optic chiasm and outside the brainstem.
* Patient can medically tolerate surgery and fSRS. The treating surgeon must deem the index lesion an appropriate target for safe resection.
* Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) ≥50 within 14 days prior to registration.
* A negative urine or serum pregnancy test (for individuals of childbearing potential) ≤14 days prior to registration.
* Patient or legally authorized representative provides study-specific informed consent before study entry. For patients treated in the U.S., authorization permitting release of personal health information is also required.

Exclusion Criteria:

\- Previous cranial radiotherapy, including whole-brain radiotherapy or stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS), to the planned resection site (index lesion). Repeat radiosurgery to the same location/lesion is not permitted on this protocol.

Note: Prior or current fSRS/SRS to other non-index lesions is allowed.

* Evidence of leptomeningeal disease.
* Any contraindication or inability to undergo MRI with contrast.
* Planned administration of cytotoxic chemotherapy or tyrosine/multi-kinase inhibitors within 3 days prior to, on the day of, or within 3 days after the completion of fSRS.

Note: Chemotherapy and immunotherapy outside of this window are allowed.
